I added `docs/ai-log/raw/` to `.gitignore`. Git now ignores the raw log, so you don't need to delete it before committing anymore.

The file was already in your repo, so the ignore rule alone wouldn't have hidden new changes to it. I also ran `git rm --cached` on it. That stages its removal from the repo but keeps your local copy, which the hook has already recreated.

To commit, stage the other two changes:

```
git add .gitignore docs/ai-log/conversations.md
```

The commit will add `conversations.md`, update `.gitignore` and remove `prompts.jsonl` from the repo. The hook will keep writing to your local copy, and git won't pick it up.
